_comment: Knowledge base for the Amazon Pharmacy voice demo. Read by server/catalog.py and surfaced through the lookup_medication and check_price tools. The Zepbound rows mirror the reference call exactly: 12.5 mg, 84-day supply, 6 mL, $50 insurance, $25 manufacturer savings. Everything else is plausible demo data chosen for coverage of the cases this demo is built to survive - mishearings, unit rendering (mg vs mcg vs units vs puffs), out-of-stock, course-based drugs, and a Schedule II boundary. PRICES ARE DEMO PLACEHOLDERS, NOT QUOTES. Validate edits with scripts/check_catalog.py.

policies.day_supply: 90-day requests dispense as an 84-day supply per insurance billing cycles; always say 'eighty-four day supply' when quoting
policies.price_disclaimer: average insurance price is an estimate based on what other customers paid; actual price may differ
policies.delivery: free two-day delivery on every order, and same-day delivery at eligible addresses
policies.prescription_transfer: offer transfer from another pharmacy when the caller shows purchase intent; the pharmacy handles the transfer, the caller does not have to call the old pharmacy
policies.new_prescription: a new prescription has to come from the prescriber, sent electronically to Amazon Pharmacy
policies.refills: refills ship automatically when auto-refill is on; otherwise the caller confirms each one in the app
policies.pillpack: PillPack sorts multiple daily medications into dated packets, at no extra cost, for callers taking several medications a day
policies.insurance: most major plans are accepted, and the cash price is shown alongside the insurance price so the caller can choose the cheaper one
policies.controlled_substances: Schedule II prescriptions cannot be transferred, cannot exceed a 30-day supply, and need a new electronic prescription from the prescriber
policies.coupons: manufacturer savings cards are applied automatically when a medication has one on file
policies.medical_advice: no dosing recommendations, no drug-interaction advice, no diagnosis - refer to the pharmacist or prescriber
policies.out_of_stock: when a medication is unavailable, say so plainly, do not suggest a substitute drug, and offer to have a pharmacist follow up
policies.cold_chain: refrigerated medications ship in an insulated cold pack with a temperature monitor, on faster service so they arrive cold
policies.signature: controlled medications and refrigerated items require a signature on delivery; everything else is left at the door
policies.po_box: post office boxes work for standard medications but not for anything requiring a signature or refrigeration
